# Founding Fuel: Consumer Behaviour & Retail — Batch 1 (2015–2020)
## Dense Observations for Synthesis

---

### ARGUMENTS FF MAKES REPEATEDLY

**1. Experience Economy > Service Economy > Product Economy**
The progression from product to service to experience is a recurring framework. Starbucks is the canonical example: "not by marketing coffee as a product...not by marketing coffee as a service...but by marketing it as an experience." The five senses are the delivery mechanism: "When the five senses are engaged and assaulted in unison, they heighten any experience."
— SOURCE: "Why you should sell your brand as an experience" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-17)

**2. Brand advocacy beats loyalty beats satisfaction**
"I yearn for brand advocates—customers who would not just be satisfied or loyal to my brand, but scream, shout and broadcast to everyone who cares to listen." Nielsen data (92% trust earned media over advertising) is cited repeatedly to establish this hierarchy.
— SOURCE: "Brand friend for life" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-22)

**3. Behavioural science principles embedded in business strategy**
Loss aversion (Zara's scarcity), decoy effect (The Economist's pricing), scarcity effect (OnePlus invites), expert bias (Sensodyne's doctor), conformity bias and fear of regret (Amazon's social proof) are cited as actionable tools companies deploy deliberately. The framing is consistently: "embed principles of behavioural science into your business and then sit back and reap rich dividends."
— SOURCE: "How Zara, Sensodyne and others use behavioural science to unlock value" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-22); "What successful companies do to win customer loyalty" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-04)

**4. Advertising is losing credibility; buzz/earned media is the replacement**
"A rising buzz is inversely proportional to the expenses a company incurs for advertising." Google's rejection of Sergio Zyman's marketing plan is presented as paradigmatic: "Their mantra was: Focus on the user and all else will follow."
— SOURCE: "Brand friend for life" by Founding Fuel (2015-03-22); "Smart strategies to get customers to actively seek out your brand communication" by Founding Fuel (2015-07-15)

**5. The customer-as-partial-employee model**
McDonald's, airlines, and e-commerce are cited as having "outsourced" work to customers "without paying them a dime" — and this raises, not lowers, satisfaction, because "complaining about bad service is tantamount to complaining against themselves."
— SOURCE: "Improve customer satisfaction at minimal cost: Convert customers into 'employees'" by Founding Fuel (2015-09-02)

**6. Proactive/anticipatory strategy beats reactive**
Amazon's anticipatory shipping, "Pay to Quit" policy, and predictive algorithms are presented as the defining edge. "The admired enterprises of today do not wait for trouble to raise their ugly heads; they pick up issues at a nascent stage."
— SOURCE: "What successful companies do to win customer loyalty" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-04)

**7. Customers now own brands emotionally, not legally**
"Legally the brand belongs to the enterprise, but emotionally its ownership rests in the hearts of customers." The "prosumer" concept — customers who produce and consume brand content — is presented as a structural shift, not a trend.
— SOURCE: "How to get customers to own your brand" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-20)

**8. Physical retail can survive e-commerce if it solves different problems**
MINISO's founder is quoted: "I firmly believe that it is the physical economy that will dominate the future as long as the exposed problems can be solved." The argument: physical retail must pivot to experience, curation, and value alignment — not price competition.
— SOURCE: "How variety store MINISO became a mega-success" by CKGSB Knowledge (2017-07-22)

**9. Big Tech is competing for attention against sleep, family, and health**
Reed Hastings's statement — "We're competing with sleep, on the margin" — is used as a portal into the ethics of engagement design. The cocaine-dealer analogy ("the first shot is always free") is introduced without irony.
— SOURCE: "A nudge against sleep and productivity" by Charles Assisi (2019-07-12)

**10. Comfort brands surge during crises; the recession playbook shifts**
In Covid: "Across America, sales are surging for comfort brands...small-batch products that in the last few years were rapidly eating up market-share...are struggling." This is tied to the mascara/lipstick effect: beauty purchases rise in downturns as low-cost indulgence.
— SOURCE: "I want my MTV" by Harsh Mall (2020-07-10); "The mascara effect" by Charles Assisi (2020-07-21)

---

### FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India's price sensitivity vs. China's aspirational spending**
"The reality is that Indian consumers, unlike Chinese customers, are not looking for a smaller smartphone, but a cheaper one." India's 47% import duty structure is identified as a structural distortion. Chinese consumers trade up faster; Indian consumers have "calculators fitted in their minds."
— SOURCE: "Why iPhone SE may lose out in India and why Amazon wants to open bookstores" by Rajesh Srivastava (2016-04-01)

**Patanjali as a distinctly Indian disruption**
Patanjali challenges FMCG orthodoxy through: no fancy MBA managers, own-channel distribution (bypassing distributor margins), 20–25% cost advantage passed to consumers, dowdy packaging read as authenticity, and Baba Ramdev's endorsement during yoga broadcasts. "For an entire generation of FMCG managers who've grown up on a different menu, the Patanjali phenomenon is proving to be a bit hard to digest."
— SOURCE: "The Patanjali phenomenon" by Indrajit Gupta (2016-02-18)

**Patanjali as cultural signal, not just brand**
Damodar Mall's hypothesis is invoked — Patanjali represents a deeper trust shift tied to generational endorsement. "In many cases, it has the ringing endorsement of the older generation in most Indian families—and that carries a lot more weight than the crores invested in advertising."
— SOURCE: "The Patanjali phenomenon" by Indrajit Gupta (2016-02-18)

**TikTok as Bharat phenomenon**
"FMCG majors, broadcasters, automobile, paints and finance companies continue to remain blissfully insulated from an app that has stormed the eyeballs of at least 200 million of their own core customers." The key distinction: TikTok democratised celebrity in small-town India, enabled by cheap data (Jio implied), not just technology.
— SOURCE: "Bharat is watching this. Is your brand watching too?" by Piyul Mukherjee (2019-07-28); "Please look now: We are changing" by Piyul Mukherjee (2019-07-28)

**TikTok as identity and modernity signal in conservative contexts**
"Modernity is defined in the clothes, but the ethos does not reach deep value systems. And this is not seen as a contradiction." Shivani Kapila from Surat — wears shorts, travels to London, makes videos on women empowerment, supported by in-laws — is offered as the archetype of this split modernity.
— SOURCE: "Please look now: We are changing" by Piyul Mukherjee (2019-07-28)

**The selfie economy reshaping Indian retail**
Mumbai retailer data: sales of lower-body apparel falling; upper-body apparel rising driven by selfie culture. Young consumers financing Rs 1,000–1,500 clothing purchases through Bajaj Finserv EMIs. "The idea of treating the body as a temple has taken root."
— SOURCE: "Death of the white shirt?" by Charles Assisi (2019-04-14)

**India's ageing population as ignored consumer segment**
India will have 340 million people above 60 by 2050. Tech design ignores them. ATM interfaces that time out before elderly users can respond are given as a concrete failure example. Joseph Coughlin's framing is invoked: "an expectations gap between what older consumers want from a product and what most of these products deliver."
— SOURCE: "The consumers technology is leaving behind" by Founding Fuel (2019-09-15)

**India's omnichannel challenge as distinctly traditional-retail problem**
Traditional retailers' dismissive term — "fit lifters" — for customers who try on in stores and buy online is noted. Most Indian traditional retailers have "turned a Nelson's eye to this change in behaviour."
— SOURCE: "Wooing the multi-channel shopper" by Founding Fuel (2015-07-22)

**Research being undervalued in Indian advertising**
"This obsession with sample size is a peculiar Indian trait." Ethnographic research is defended against both the gut-instinct bias of creative teams and the data-fetishism of tech companies. Future Group's "Future Ideas" cell is cited as exceptional practice.
— SOURCE: "Building consumer empathy" by Founding Fuel (2015-10-24)

---

### FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, MENTAL MODELS

**Behavioural economics/science** (used throughout): loss aversion, decoy effect, scarcity effect, expert bias, conformity bias, fear of regret, effort justification, social proof, hot buttons.
— SOURCE: "How Zara, Sensodyne and others use behavioural science to unlock value" (2015-06-22); "What successful companies do to win customer loyalty" (2015-05-04)

**The Experience Economy** (Pine & Gilmore implicit): Product → Service → Experience progression.
— SOURCE: "Why you should sell your brand as an experience" (2015-06-17)

**Cool Brand Framework**: Three-axis model — (1) delivers on promise, (2) boosts self-esteem/confidence, (3) helps project identity to peers. BMW is the test case.
— SOURCE: "A Brand Is Not Enough. Create a Cool Brand" (2015-07-30)

**Prosumer concept**: Customers as producers + consumers of brand content. Airbnb, eBay, Uber as paradigms.
— SOURCE: "How to get customers to own your brand" (2015-05-20)

**Kahneman**: Experience vs. memory distinction in travel/consumption; the "riddle of experience versus memory" TED Talk. Also Bias, Blindness and How We Truly Think series referenced.
— SOURCE: "Stories, not places, inspire us to travel" by Indranil Chakraborty (2017-04-04)

**Ethnographic research** as superior to survey data in consumer understanding. Sample size obsession critiqued.
— SOURCE: "Building consumer empathy" by Founding Fuel (2015-10-24)

**Nudge theory** (implicit): "The harder we try to be productive, the easier it is for us to be nudged into something against our interests."
— SOURCE: "A nudge against sleep and productivity" by Charles Assisi (2019-07-12)

**Kendall Haven / Story Proof**: "Story, somehow transforms simple stone walls into a vibrant, emotionally charged, meaningful, and exciting landscape." Applied to tourism marketing.
— SOURCE: "Stories, not places, inspire us to travel" by Indranil Chakraborty (2017-04-04)

**Lipstick Effect / Mascara Effect**: Leonard Lauder's insight: "When times are bad, consumption of inexpensive cosmetics rises." Extended with Yad Vashem documentation of beauty rituals in Holocaust concentration camps.
— SOURCE: "The mascara effect" by Charles Assisi (2020-07-21)

**Gerd Gigerenzer** referenced in context of algorithmic nudging and decision-making.
— SOURCE: "A nudge against sleep and productivity" by Charles Assisi (2019-07-12)

---

### WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**Traditional advertising's ROI and relevance**
"Advertising requires huge investments. But as these findings suggest, these investments are governed by the law of diminishing returns." Mass advertising that interrupts (Ronaldo penalty kick scenario) creates negative brand association.
— SOURCE: "Brand friend for life" (2015-03-22); "Smart strategies to get customers to actively seek out your brand communication" (2015-07-15)

**The "data kills qualitative research" narrative**
"Even as this old rivalry plays out, the new battleground is between being data-driven versus the old direct consumer immersion model...nothing could be further from the truth." Banks, e-commerce companies and telcos are explicitly named as over-confident in data.
— SOURCE: "Building consumer empathy" by Founding Fuel (2015-10-24)

**The "e-commerce kills physical retail" narrative**
"Perhaps it would be more correct to say that it is forcing change." MINISO's success is offered as evidence that constrained, experiential physical retail can thrive.
— SOURCE: "How variety store MINISO became a mega-success" by CKGSB Knowledge (2017-07-22)

**Marketers dismissing TikTok as a hinterland fad**
"Business As Usual marketers are blissfully insulated from what's happening on TikTok, an app that has at least 200 million of their own core customers hooked." The dismissal is characterised as class-based blindness — "We believe that TikTok is for the Buntys and Bablis of Bharat."
— SOURCE: "Bharat is watching this. Is your brand watching too?" by Piyul Mukherjee (2019-07-28)

**The assumption that Patanjali will peter out**
"Some believe that the Patanjali phenomenon will soon start to peter out." FF doesn't fully agree. "It isn't just about Ramdev's magic or about the power of herbal and Ayurveda alone. It is much deeper."
— SOURCE: "The Patanjali phenomenon" by Indrajit Gupta (2016-02-18)

**Assumption that attention spans are simply "shortening"**
"That may seem like an obvious explanation. But there is a deeper cause." Damodar Mall argues Netflix abandonment is about switching cost elimination, not cognitive decline: "You're just practising your ability to make more choices."
— SOURCE: "What's playing next? And where?" by Founding Fuel (2020-08-10)

**Big Tech's ethics of engagement**
"We aren't very different from cocaine peddlers. The first shot is always free." FF notes the breakup debate is alive in the US but "has not gained public attention yet" in India — and names India as "the largest market for these companies" outside the US.
— SOURCE: "A nudge against sleep and productivity" by Charles Assisi (2019-07-12)

---

### COMPANIES, LEADERS, EXAMPLES — CELEBRATED OR CRITIQUED

**Celebrated:**
- **Amazon**: Anticipatory shopping, personalization algorithms, "Pay to Quit" as proactive HR. Amazon's "phygital" logistics praised.
 — SOURCE: "What successful companies do to win customer loyalty" (2015-05-04)
- **Google**: Rejection of Zyman's plan; product-led growth as brand strategy paradigm.
 — SOURCE: "Brand friend for life" (2015-03-22)
- **Starbucks**: Canonical five-sense experience delivery. "Arguably regarded as the purveyor of the world's best coffee" — achieved through experience framing, not product claims.
 — SOURCE: "Why you should sell your brand as an experience" (2015-06-17)
- **Zara**: Fast fashion as loss aversion + scarcity engine. Also cited by Paper Boat founders for seasonal product strategy.
 — SOURCE: "How Zara, Sensodyne and others use behavioural science to unlock value" (2015-06-22); "Paper Boat: Riding on a wave of nostalgia" (2016-09-22)
- **Airbnb / Uber / eBay**: Prosumer/platform models with near-complete ceding of brand control to customers.
 — SOURCE: "How to get customers to own your brand" (2015-05-20)
- **Tesla**: Not selling cars but "informing and educating"; Tesla Stores as brand-building rather than sales venues. "A Tesla car by design is not a car—it is an iPhone on wheels."
 — SOURCE: "How green is Tesla Model 3?" by Rajesh Srivastava (2016

# Consumer Behaviour & Retail — BATCH 2: Dense Observations

---

## REPEATED ARGUMENTS ACROSS FF COVERAGE

**1. The "hidden motives" argument: stated reasons ≠ real reasons**
"Conventional wisdom holds that consumers buy green goods... in order to 'help the environment.' But we must think harder" — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #205: Why do people 'go green'?" by Founding Fuel (2020-10-15)

"We assume users are rational, needs are explicit, and decisions are logical. In reality, decisions...are driven by fear, guilt, pride, and the need for control." — SOURCE: "Why Emotions Are First Principles in Product Strategy" by Shrinath V (2025-11-04)

**2. Offline behaviour patterns transfer to online contexts; data alone cannot explain them**
"Maybe the difference had less to do with product design, and more to do with the kinds of offline behaviours users were transferring to an online context... COD restores a sense of control... Payment before delivery feels like a leap." — SOURCE: "Nuance is the new differentiator" by Shrinath V (2025-06-25)

**3. Trust must be earned differently in non-metro India; it is a structural prerequisite, not an afterthought**
"Middle India is new to many of these online transactions that rely on implicit trust... trust needs to be earned especially for new solutions that involve a different process, lack a human interface and require the use of new technology." — SOURCE: "The Middle India consumer" by Founding Fuel (2022-11-08)

**4. Speed/convenience culture has costs that are underexamined**
"Hurry took its place at the dinner table during the Industrial Revolution... Today, most meals are little more than refuelling pit stops." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #616: Slow food" by Founding Fuel (2022-03-30)

On Zomato's 10-minute delivery: "Its critics pointed to the risks and stress the delivery partners are put under with such promises." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #616: Slow food" by Founding Fuel (2022-03-30)

**5. Price-based competition is a trap, not a strategy**
"Selling based on price is like heroin. The short-term gain is fantastic, but the more you do it, the harder it becomes to kick the habit." (citing Simon Sinek) — SOURCE: "FF Daily #463: The price game" by Founding Fuel (2021-09-02)

**6. Consumer behaviour changes in India lag visible infrastructure changes; deep contextual reading required**
"Behaviour is flattened into metrics, and context becomes optional. But people don't live in clean funnels." — SOURCE: "Nuance is the new differentiator" by Shrinath V (2025-06-25)

**7. The pandemic as permanent inflection point in consumer habits**
"What is painfully obvious to most of us now is that our lives have changed forever." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #213: FF Recommends | Personal mobility" by Founding Fuel (2020-10-24)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**The Middle India consumer as a distinct, underserved analytical category**
"For long, organised retailers stuck to metros and Tier 1 and Tier 2 towns. This is among the first indications of the huge opportunity in Bharat." On Zudio opening in Jharsuguda, Dimapur, Imphal, Pathankot, Gorakhpur — SOURCE: "Noel Tata's brahmastra" by Indrajit Gupta (2023-08-28)

**India's consumer bazaar logic: technology gets locally improvised, not adopted as designed**
"A sugarcane juice vendor with a QR code. A tailoring shop that takes orders via WhatsApp voice notes... use cases are not always discovered by companies designing products or services. They're discovered by users." — SOURCE: "From Bazaar to Breakthrough" by Shrinath V (2025-06-18)

CRBTs as early digital self-expression for first-time mobile users: "For many first-time mobile users, this was a rare space for digital self-expression... A rare space for digital self-expression. CRBTs offered a sense of presence in a world where apps were still English-first and interfaces rarely reflected them." — SOURCE: "From Bazaar to Breakthrough" by Shrinath V (2025-06-18)

**The nostalgia economy — Indian food and memory**
"Ghar ka khana, to my mind, you remember the most because it is made with emotions. It is unconditional, and in some sense it's free. Bahar ka khana is commerce. It is cooked for profit, but at home it is cooked for care." — SOURCE: "On the menu: The changing attitude towards home cooking" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-29)

"The nostalgic value" of ghar ka khana only surfaces when you "move away from home" — SOURCE: "On the menu: The changing attitude towards home cooking" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-29)

**India's mango and millet consumption as windows into broader shifts: from rural staple to urban aspiration and back**
"Millets essentially ended up as poor people's food. Now we are coming full circle." — SOURCE: "FF Life: The golden seed" by Founding Fuel (2023-10-06)

Millets connect individual health, climate resilience, and food security simultaneously: "Three factors driving the renewed interest in millets—production with fewer resources, resilience to climate change, and wellness through food." — SOURCE: "FF Life: The golden seed" by Founding Fuel (2023-10-06)

**Indian diaspora beauty as a commercially legible nostalgia play**
"These sorts of ingredients are known as adaptogens in Western culture, but for Roy, 'these are just ingredients I grew up with.'" Aavrani's packaging evokes "the bright golden yellow of the mangoes her grandmother would cut for her" — SOURCE: "An Indian beauty upstart in the West" by Aparajita Bhattacharyya (2021-05-31)

**Blue-collar trust in India is broken; fintech must rebuild it with radical transparency**
"Most blue-collar workers hardly knew they were getting a pension accrual and had no idea how to check the balance. There were also cases of contractors withholding these pay-outs." Smartstaff's PF visibility became a "sticky feature from a trust perspective" — SOURCE: "The Middle India consumer" by Founding Fuel (2022-11-08)

**India's GST and logistics infrastructure unlocking retail hinterland**
"With the GST regime, better road infrastructure, and modern third-party warehouses and transportation systems, it has become a lot easier to build a more predictable supply chain... penetrate deeper into the hinterland." — SOURCE: "Noel Tata's brahmastra" by Indrajit Gupta (2023-08-28)

**EV adoption in India: two-wheelers and three-wheelers ahead of four-wheelers; apartment society charging politics a real barrier**
"He had a hard time negotiating installing a charger in his society and had to charge his scooter at his home on the fifth floor." — SOURCE: "How to choose the right electric scooter: A buying guide" by C S Swaminathan (2021-11-20)

"Electric cars have lagged well behind scooters, accounting for only about one in fifty cars sold today." — SOURCE: "What they don't tell you about EVs in India" by Pranav Srivilasan (2024-09-27)

---

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, AND MENTAL MODELS

**Simon Sinek — Start With Why**
Price addiction as a downward spiral: "selling based on price is like heroin" — SOURCE: "FF Daily #463: The price game" by Founding Fuel (2021-09-02)

**Simler & Hanson — The Elephant in the Brain**
Conspicuous altruism: "Prius owners are signaling their prosocial attitude... It's an act of conspicuous altruism." Status as the hidden motive behind green consumption — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #205: Why do people 'go green'?" by Founding Fuel (2020-10-15)

**Carl Honore — In Praise of Slow**
The Slow Food movement as antidote to fast food: "Slow Food also preaches 'eco-gastronomy'—the notion that eating well can, and should, go hand in hand with protecting the environment." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #616: Slow food" by Founding Fuel (2022-03-30)

**Paco Underhill — Why We Buy**
Sign-reading behaviour and context: fast food solo diners read table tents at 25% vs. 2% in family restaurants. Context determines attention — SOURCE: "FF Daily #537: Fast food and slow reading" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-01)

**Eric S. Raymond — The Cathedral and the Bazaar**
Applied to Indian tech innovation: India as a "bazaar" model of technology adoption — improvised, user-led, bottom-up — SOURCE: "From Bazaar to Breakthrough" by Shrinath V (2025-06-18)

**GP Cachon's retail typology (Wharton)**
"Turns Retailers" (low markup, high inventory turns) vs "Earns Retailers" — applied to Zudio — SOURCE: "Noel Tata's brahmastra" by Indrajit Gupta (2023-08-28)

**Parkinson's Law (invoked with pandemic twist)**
"In a pandemic era twist to Parkinson's Law, work seems to expand well beyond the available time." — SOURCE: "FF Life: Smarter living" by Founding Fuel (2022-07-16)

**Emotion as first principles in product strategy**
"When you grasp what people carry emotionally, your product lens sharpens. You stop building what makes sense and start building what makes meaning." — SOURCE: "Why Emotions Are First Principles in Product Strategy" by Shrinath V (2025-11-04)

**Customer journey rebundling (Sephora model)**
"The paradox of customer journey rebundling is that it works best when it doesn't feel engineered at all." — SOURCE: "Book Extract: From customer journeys to integrated experiences" by Founding Fuel (2025-09-17)

**India Stack / DigiLocker as seamless infrastructure**
Described as "magical" — "Within seconds I had the digital copy of [my driving license]." — SOURCE: "A digital immigrant's initiation into the digital-first world" by Founding Fuel (2021-11-29)

---

## WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**Skeptical of: speed as inherent virtue in food delivery**
"What kind of food can be delivered from the station to home in 10 minutes?" — SOURCE: "FF Insights #616: Slow food" by Founding Fuel (2022-03-30)

**Skeptical of: stated green motives at face value**
The Prius experiment shows green consumption is partly status performance, not just environmental concern — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #205: Why do people 'go green'?" by Founding Fuel (2020-10-15)

**Skeptical of: "driver behaviour" as sole cause of road accidents**
"Seeking to find a single cause for a crash is a fundamentally flawed approach... attributing it all to human error is so much more convenient for everyone." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #537: Fast food and slow reading" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-01)

**Skeptical of: Bollywood's theatrical model post-pandemic**
"Is this change in user behaviour likely to be long drawn? If viewers continue to shun theatrical releases, it could have serious implications for the structure and construct of the Bollywood film industry." — SOURCE: "Bollywood's wakeup call" by Indrajit Gupta (2022-05-31)

**Skeptical of: over-reliance on data and AI in consumer research**
"With AI tools now entering the research process, that gap [between data and human behaviour] may quietly widen." — SOURCE: "Nuance is the new differentiator" by Shrinath V (2025-06-25)

**Skeptical of: tech-first framing for every consumer problem**
"The seniors didn't want apps... Smartwatches and sensors didn't work either. They forgot to wear them... Wearing a smartwatch felt like being monitored. It wasn't restoring anything." — SOURCE: "Why Emotions Are First Principles in Product Strategy" by Shrinath V (2025-11-04)

**Skeptical of: Ola Electric's quality culture**
"Ola, frankly—unfortunately, the company doesn't have a quality culture. It's all about getting products out fast, really, not going through proper validation. It's catching up with them." — SOURCE: "AMA on EVs with Hormazd Sorabjee and Pranav S: 22 Takeaways" by Founding Fuel (2024-10-18)

**Skeptical of: Shein's model despite its scale**
"Its model also has been roundly criticised for harming the environment, for relying on dyes that don't meet standards and using poor quality, disposable and unsustainable rayon fabric." — SOURCE: "Noel Tata's brahmastra" by Indrajit Gupta (2023-08-28)

**Skeptical of: "deep tech" as the only legitimate investor narrative**
"Investor questions circled one theme: 'Where's the deep tech?'" — FF positions SilverGenie's human-centric model as the correct insight that investors were missing — SOURCE: "Why Emotions Are First Principles in Product Strategy" by Shrinath V (2025-11-04)

**Skeptical of: buying a car in the pandemic/post-pandemic era**
"Save the money and put it in the bank. Buy a good pair of Nike or Adidas instead and take an Uber or Ola when you need a ride." — SOURCE: "FF Recommends: How to maintain and buy an automobile" by Founding Fuel (2021-06-12)

**Skeptical of: range extenders as Wi-Fi solution**
"Outdated idea!" — SOURCE: "FF Recommends: Mesh Networks" by Charles Assisi (2021-11-09)

---

## COMPANIES, LEADERS, AND EXAMPLES — CELEBRATED OR CRITIQUED

**CELEBRATED:**

*Zudio / Trent / Noel Tata*
"Zudio is rapidly spreading its wings across more than 120 locations... What was the inspiration behind Zudio? It seems to have taken a leaf out of its Spanish partner Inditex." — SOURCE: "Noel Tata's brahmastra" by Indrajit Gupta (2023-08-28)

*Sephora*
"Sephora understands that winning the right to serve the customer doesn't stop with dominating individual steps across the journey; it requires orchestrating the entire experience." — SOURCE: "Book Extract: From customer journeys to integrated experiences" by Founding Fuel (2025-09-17)

*Razorpay*
"Razorpay made it a goal to win trust by providing useful content to small businesses... they became a trusted voice... Razorpay would be the first port of call." — SOURCE: "The Middle India consumer" by Founding Fuel (2022-11-08)

*Meesho*
"Meesho leverages the connections and local recognition of its women entrepreneurs to introduce end consumers to the company's marketplace technology platform." — SOURCE: "The Middle India consumer" by Founding Fuel (2022-11-08)

*Aavrani*
Celebrated as a successful translation of Indian cultural knowledge into luxury Western skincare: "$1 million+ in revenue in 2019, and anticipates growing 5x." — SOURCE: "An Indian beauty upstart in the West" by Aparajita Bhattacharyya (2021-05-31)

*Ather 450*
Featured as a thoughtful EV purchase: "I zeroed in on the Ather 450. It was delivered in mid 2019 and since then I have put in about 5,000 km on it." — SOURCE: "How to choose the right electric scooter: A buying guide" by C S Swaminathan (2021-11-20)

*SilverGenie / Poulomi Bhattacharya*
Celebrated for correctly reading the emotional driver (adult-child guilt) behind elder care purchasing — SOURCE: "Why Emotions Are First Principles in Product Strategy" by Shrinath V (2025-11-04)

*
